validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Reproduced end-to-end twice in a real browser against $PREVIEW_URL on the demo budget, and the mechanism was confirmed by three scratch vitest runs that drove the actual factory closures with stubbed send/fetchSpreadsheetQueryData, printing the real pre-fix axes, and then a fourth that ran the proposed narrowing helper and printed the corrected axes. The proposed fix is not argued from reading: its output was observed. Below 100 only for blast radius - GetCardData.tsx is a second caller whose output this change alters but which I did not exercise in a browser, and the Payee/Account/Interval splits were traced through groupBySelections source rather than each driven in the UI.
validated_work_order.understanding: Reproduced exactly as reported on the demo budget at $PREVIEW_URL (http://localhost:3001), headless Chromium via Playwright 1.61.1, twice in this run. Steps: open /reports/custom (fresh Custom Report, Mode=Total, Split=Category, Type=Payment, Interval=Monthly), click 'Data Table' in the topbar, click 'Unselect All' in the category selector, tick only the 'Bills' group checkbox, then Options -> 'Show empty rows'. With Show empty rows OFF the table correctly shows only the five Bills categories (Cell -150.00, Internet -120.00, Mortgage -2,400.00, Water -180.00, Power -200.00) totalling -3,050.00. Turning Show empty rows ON adds back every unchecked category in the entire budget at 0.00: the whole 'Usual Expenses' group with Food, Restaurants, Entertainment, Clothing, General, Gift, Medical and Savings; the 'Income' group with Starting Balances, Misc and Income; and 'Uncategorized & Off budget' with Uncategorized, Transfers and Off budget - 23 extra rows. The applied filter chip reads 'category one of [Cell, Internet, Mortgage, 2 more items...]', so the selection is correctly recorded and correctly applied to the amounts; only the row axis is wrong, and the totals row stayed at -3,050.00 throughout, confirming the amounts were always correctly filtered. I varied the selection away from a whole group, since the reporter's phrasing ('only selecting a category group') could have implied a group-specific defect: ticking a single category ('Food') reproduces identically, with Restaurants, Entertainment, Clothing, General, Gift, Medical, Savings and all of Bills and Income appearing at 0.00. I also drove Split=Group with the same Bills-only selection, which reproduces too - 'Usual Expenses 0.00', 'Income 0.00' and 'Uncategorized & Off budget 0.00' are all present after the fix should have removed them. So the defect is in the selection filter generally and reaches the category split, the group split and the table view alike. Console output carried no application errors; the only console errors were React's 'Encountered two children with the same key' warning, which reproduces on the untouched page before any interaction and is pre-existing.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The report's category selection reaches the amounts but never reaches the row axis, and it misses the axis in two distinct places because the axis has two independently-derived halves. The selection arrives only as a `category oneOf [...]` query filter applied inside makeQuery, so an unselected category correctly contributes 0 to every amount. Meanwhile custom-spreadsheet.ts:87 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:39 both call categoryLists(categories) on the raw unfiltered `categories` from useCategories(). categoryLists returns two halves from that one call: `categoryList`, built from `categories.list` (ReportOptions.ts:387-401), and `categoryGroup`, built as a verbatim copy `[...categories.grouped, uncategorizedGroup]` (ReportOptions.ts:403-405). Everything the table actually renders comes from the second half - grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94 maps `categoryGroup` for the group rows, and lines 110-111 map each group's nested `categories`, which are the embedded arrays populated server-side by getCategories (app.ts:190, `list = categoryGroups.flatMap(g => g.categories)`) and are never derived from `categories.list`. So a fix that narrows only `list` cannot reach the table view at all; and groupBySelections' 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' cases (ReportOptions.ts:427-451) both build their axis from `categoryGroup`, so they miss it too. This is why the prior plan's grouped-spreadsheet.ts edit was inert. filterEmptyRows is the only thing that ever reconciled the two sides, and it does so destructively: with showEmpty false it drops every zero row, which incidentally drops the unselected categories and hides the defect; with showEmpty true it returns true unconditionally (filterEmptyRows.ts:24), so all the unselected rows survive at 0.00. 'Show empty rows' is thus not overriding the selection - it is removing the only filter that was hiding the fact that the selection never reached the axis. The same asymmetry already has a correct implementation elsewhere: fetchBudgetData (the Type=Budgeted path) calls filterCategoriesByConditions to narrow its category list before use (budgetDataQuery.ts:203), which is why the axis and the amounts agree there.
validated_work_order.approach: Narrow BOTH halves of the category axis at the point the spreadsheets build it, using the existing filterCategoriesByConditions helper in budgetDataQuery.ts rather than a new predicate. Add one exported helper, narrowCategoriesByConditions(categories, conditions, conditionsOp), that calls filterCategoriesByConditions to get the surviving `list`, then derives the surviving id set and maps `categories.grouped` to a new array whose each group's `categories` is intersected with that set, dropping groups left with an empty `categories` array. Both factories call this once and pass the narrowed `{list, grouped}` to categoryLists. Narrowing `grouped` - not `list` - is what makes the table view correct: grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94-111 and the 'Group'/'CategoryGroup' branches of groupBySelections read only the grouped half, so a list-only narrowing leaves the reporter's exact symptom fully intact. Two deliberate details. First, the helper returns `categories` unchanged (by identity) when filterCategoriesByConditions returns its input unchanged, which is what it does for an absent, empty, non-category, or unsafely-interpretable condition set; that preserves the conservative 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' fallback, and it also means a group that is legitimately empty in an unfiltered report is not silently dropped. Second, the synthetic `uncategorizedGroup` is appended by categoryLists itself after whatever `grouped` it is given (ReportOptions.ts:403-405), so it is out of reach of this narrowing by construction and the Uncategorized/Off budget block survives - it is out_of_scope here and must not be filtered away. Keep passing the unfiltered `categories.list`/`categories.grouped` to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData in both factories, so the query-side filter is untouched and both sides are computed from the same expression. Keep filterEmptyRows unchanged; it is correct for its job and is only ever exposed by this bug. Do not special-case groupBy - the defect is upstream of the split, in the shared axis.

files.change: Add and export `narrowCategoriesByConditions(categories, conditions, conditionsOp)` next to the existing filterCategoriesByConditions. It takes `{ list: CategoryEntity[]; grouped: CategoryGroupEntity[] }` and returns the same shape, narrowed by conditions. Implementation: call `filterCategoriesByConditions(categories.list, categories.grouped, conditions, conditionsOp)` to get `list`; if the returned array is `categories.list` by identity (the helper's documented signal that no condition narrowed anything - absent, empty, non-category, or unsafely interpretable), return `categories` unchanged and do nothing else. Otherwise build `const keep = new Set(list.map(c => c.id))`, map `categories.grouped` to `categories.grouped.map(g => ({ ...g, categories: (g.categories ?? []).filter(c => keep.has(c.id)) }))`, then `.filter(g => g.categories.length > 0)` to drop groups emptied by the narrowing, and return `{ list, grouped }`. The identity check is load-bearing, not an optimisation: without it a genuinely empty category group would be dropped from every unfiltered report in the product.
files.why: Both spreadsheet factories need the identical narrowing, and putting it beside the existing helper keeps one definition of 'which categories does this condition select' in the codebase instead of two that can drift.

No application code was modified before the reproduction; git status showed only the untracked plan/ directory. The reproduction was run twice in this session with identical results.
Step 1 - fresh /reports/custom: Mode=Total, Split=Category, Type=Payment, Interval=Monthly. Applied filter chip: none (all categories selected).
Step 2 - clicked 'Data Table' in the topbar to reach table view.

Step 3 - clicked 'Unselect All'; then ticked only the 'Bills' group checkbox. The category selector's 19 checkboxes map 1:1 to labels: index 0 'Usual Expenses', 1 'Food' ... 8 'Savings', 9 'Bills', 10 'Cell' ... 14 'Power', 15 'Income', 16-18. Applied filter chip read 'category one of [Cell, Internet, Mortgage, 2 more items...]' - the selection is correctly recorded.

Step 4 (control) - Show empty rows OFF, #list innerText was exactly: 'Bills | -3,050.00 | -435.71 / Cell | -150.00 | -21.43 / Internet | -120.00 | -17.14 / Mortgage | -2,400.00 | -342.86 / Water | -180.00 | -25.71 / Power | -200.00 | -28.57'. Correct - only the five selected Bills categories.

Mechanism confirmed by scratch vitest runs against unmodified code, driving the real factory closures with stubbed boundaries (vi.mock of '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection' returning { filters: [] } and of './fetchSpreadsheetQueryData' returning { assets: [], debts: [] }), asserting on the rows that reach setData. This harness works and is the basis for tests[0]; the earlier plan's test called categoryLists/groupBySelections directly and so exercised none of the changed code. Command: yarn workspace @actual-app/web exec vitest run src/components/reports/spreadsheets/__scratch.test.ts. Fixture: Food and Rent in g-usual, Cell in g-bills; conditions [{field:'category',op:'oneOf',value:['c-cell']}]; showEmpty true. Result: 4 passed, and the axes printed were - createCustomSpreadsheet groupBy='Category': [Food, Rent, Cell, Uncategorized, Off budget, Transfers]; groupBy='Group': [Usual Expenses, Bills, Uncategorized & Off budget]; createGroupedSpreadsheet: groups [Usual Expenses, Bills, Uncategorized & Off budget] with nested [[Food, Rent], [Cell], [Uncategorized, Transfers, Off budget]]; conditions=[] control: [Food, Rent, Cell, Uncategorized, Off budget, Transfers]. The Category axis still contains both unchecked categories AND the grouped axis still contains both groups on unmodified code - which is the direct proof that narrowing `list` alone could not have fixed either the table view or the Group split, and that both halves must be narrowed.

Proposed fix verified, not merely argued: a fourth scratch run applied the exact narrowCategoriesByConditions shape specified in files[0] (filterCategoriesByConditions for `list`, then a keep-set intersection over each group's embedded categories, dropping emptied groups) and printed the corrected axes through the real categoryLists/groupBySelections: Category ['Cell','Uncategorized','Off budget','Transfers']; Group ['Bills','Uncategorized & Off budget']; groupedData nested [['Cell'],['Uncategorized','Transfers','Off budget']]; groupBySelections('Group', ...) ['Bills','Uncategorized & Off budget']. Controls printed unchanged as required: conditions=[] gave Category ['Food','Rent','Cell','Uncategorized','Off budget','Transfers'] and Group ['Usual Expenses','Bills','Uncategorized & Off budget']; a 'hasTags' condition (unsupported) gave the same unfiltered Category and Group axes; a category_group 'is g-bills' condition gave Category ['Cell',...] and Group ['Bills',...]. A fifth scratch run checked the empty-group edge case: with the identity guard, conditions=[] preserves a group whose categories array is [] ('Bills','Empty Group'), while an actual narrowing drops it ('Bills'). Both scratch files were deleted after the run; git status is clean apart from the untracked plan/ directory.

Console/network during the browser reproduction: no application errors and no failed requests attributable to this bug. The only console errors were two instances of React's 'Encountered two children with the same key' warning, which reproduce on the untouched page before any interaction and are pre-existing.

Code corroboration, read after the reproduction: CustomReport.tsx:267 computes `selectedCategories` from the filter conditions and passes it only to ReportSidebar for rendering the checkboxes, while createGroupedSpreadsheet (line 515) and createCustomSpreadsheet (line 551) both receive the raw unfiltered `categories` from useCategories() (line 152). categoryLists (ReportOptions.ts:381-408) derives its two axis halves from different inputs: categoryList from `categories.list` (lines 387-401) and categoryGroup as a verbatim `[...categories.grouped, uncategorizedGroup]` (lines 403-405). grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94 maps categoryGroup for group rows and lines 110-111 map each group's nested categories. ReportTableList.tsx:28-31 selects data.groupedData when groupBy === 'Category', and ReportTable.tsx:159 renders id="list" - the exact element the e2e case asserts against. groupBySelections (ReportOptions.ts:412-473): 'Category' and 'Interval' read categoryList; 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' both read categoryGroup; 'Payee' and 'Account' read payees/accounts and are unaffected. The selection reaches the amounts only as a query filter inside makeQuery via fetchSpreadsheetQueryData, so unselected categories correctly contribute 0. filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:24) is the only thing that ever hid this: `return !showEmpty ? showHide : true` drops zero rows when showEmpty is off, incidentally dropping the unselected categories too.

Corroborating asymmetry in the same flow: the Type=Budgeted path already does this correctly. fetchSpreadsheetQueryData routes totalBudgeted to fetchBudgetData, which calls filterCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:203-208) to narrow the category list before building anything. That helper is the correct, already-tested implementation of exactly the narrowing this fix needs, and it already carries the conservative 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' fallback (budgetDataQuery.ts:106-108). Reusing it is why the approach does not invent a second predicate.

alternatives_considered.approach: Narrow only `categories.list` (what the rejected v1 plan specified) and leave `grouped` untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Structurally inert, and this is the objection the plan review raised against v1. categoryLists builds categoryGroup as a verbatim copy of `categories.grouped`, and each group's nested `categories` are the embedded arrays populated server-side by getCategories (app.ts:190) - neither is derived from `list`. Everything the Split=Category table view renders comes from that second half (grouped-spreadsheet.ts:94, 110-111), as do the 'Group' and 'CategoryGroup' branches of groupBySelections. Confirmed empirically: on unmodified code the closure-driven axis test prints Food and Rent in both the Category axis and the Group axis, and groupedData contains Usual Expenses with nested [Food, Rent]. Narrowing `list` alone would have fixed the bar/line/donut graphs and left the reporter's exact table-view symptom and both group rows fully intact.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it inside filterEmptyRows - make showEmpty-aware filtering also drop rows belonging to unselected categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That treats the symptom. filterEmptyRows only sees a GroupedEntity and its flag; it has no knowledge of the selection conditions, so honouring the selection there would mean threading the whole condition set through a function whose job is a zero/nonzero test. It would also leave the axis itself wrong - every unselected category would still be computed, summed into totals and handed to the legend and the graph on every render, and any other consumer of the axis would keep seeing the phantom rows. The debugger rule is to fix what produces the bad value, and the bad value is the row axis.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix it in CustomReport.tsx by passing selectedCategories into the spreadsheet factories instead of the full categories.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tempting and much smaller, but wrong in two ways. First, useSelectedCategories (CustomReport.tsx:73-113) only understands a 'category' field with is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf and deliberately returns the FULL list for every other condition shape - including category_group conditions, text operators, and the multiple-category-condition case that isComplexCategoryCondition exists to flag. So this would narrow the axis for simple selections and silently do nothing for the complex ones, an inconsistency users would hit and could not explain. Second, categories.grouped is still needed for the Group split and for per-group rows, so the prop would have to be split in two anyway - which is the same shape as the helper being added, but in the wrong layer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Filter inside categoryLists() in ReportOptions.ts, since both factories call it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: categoryLists takes only { list, grouped } and no conditions, so filtering there would require changing its signature to accept the conditions - turning a pure shape helper into one that silently drops rows based on a second input. Its existing sibling callers and its single-responsibility shape (build the three axis lists plus the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget/Transfers rows) would be lost, and its unit tests would have to grow condition fixtures. Narrowing at the two factories that own the spreadsheet inputs, via one shared helper, keeps categoryLists pure.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the row filter as a new, narrower predicate local to custom-spreadsheet.ts, handling only the category oneOf/is/isNot/notOneOf shape.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Duplicates filterCategoriesByConditions, which already implements exactly this and is already covered by budgetDataQuery.test.ts (category, category_group, oneOf, text operators, combined and/or). A second predicate would drift from it and would have no equivalent of its 'cannot safely interpret -> do not filter' guard, which is the safety property that keeps complex-condition reports from silently losing rows.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop groups whose categories are all filtered out, without the identity guard on an unnarrowed condition set.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This silently deletes any group that is legitimately empty in an unfiltered report - a user with an empty group would see it disappear from every custom report in the product, a behaviour change unrelated to this bug and with no coverage in the suite. Guarding on `list === categories.list` (which is exactly what filterCategoriesByConditions returns when it declines to narrow) makes the rebuild happen only when something was actually narrowed. Verified in a scratch run: with the guard, conditions=[] preserves a group with categories: [], while a real narrowing drops it.

risks: Over-narrowing is the real hazard. filterCategoriesByConditions returns its input unchanged when it cannot safely interpret a condition, and that fallback is load-bearing: it is what keeps reports using complex category conditions (the isComplexCategoryCondition set in CustomReport.tsx - multiple category conditions, category_group conditions, contains/doesNotContain/matches/hasTags/hasAnyTag) rendering every row they render today. The new tests must pin that fallback explicitly (AC-4), or the fix trades one wrong report for a worse one. The identity guard described in files[0] is what carries this property through the new helper, and it is easy to drop in implementation - AC-4 and AC-10 exist to catch exactly that.

Dropping emptied groups is a second way to over-narrow, and it is new behaviour that filterCategoriesByConditions has no analogue for. A group whose categories are all filtered out disappears entirely rather than rendering at 0.00. That is the intended reading of the reporter's request, but it is a judgement call, and it is why the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget block must be left untouched (AC-9) - it is appended by categoryLists after the narrowing and so is safe by construction, but an implementer who 'helpfully' also filtered it would remove a block the reporter never complained about.

Two factories change and the second is load-bearing for the reported symptom. In Split=Category the table renders data.groupedData (ReportTableList.tsx:28-31), which comes from createGroupedSpreadsheet. An implementer who edits only custom-spreadsheet.ts will see graphs corrected and the table still wrong, and may conclude the fix failed. files[2] states this explicitly for the next planner.

Two callers exist and both are affected. GetCardData.tsx (lines 127 and 146) calls the same two factories for dashboard report widgets, passing its own `categories` prop and the saved report's conditions. Because the fix lives inside the factories, dashboard widgets are corrected by the same change and need no edit - but this change alters dashboard widget output, which is outside what the reporter described. It is the correct behaviour (a widget showing a filtered report should not render unselected rows) and the shared-function argument is what makes it right, but it should be a conscious acceptance rather than a surprise at review. I did not exercise this path in a browser within this run.

The Budgeted path shares the helper. Type=Budgeted already narrowed its own axis inside fetchBudgetData; both axes now run through filterCategoriesByConditions. The narrowing is applied to the axis only, and the query call is left on the unfiltered categories, so Budgeted's data path is untouched - but AC-7 exists to confirm this empirically rather than by argument.

Low-confidence residual: I verified Split=Category (table and graph) and Split=Group in the browser with Type=Payment. I did not separately drive CategoryGroup, Interval, Payee, Account, Deposit or Net in the UI; CategoryGroup and Interval follow from the same narrowed halves (traced in groupBySelections), and Payee and Account are provably untouched because their axes come from payees/accounts and never from categories. AC-6 is scoped to the four category-derived splits for exactly this reason and names the tests that check them.
out_of_scope: The synthetic Uncategorized / Off budget / Transfers rows that categoryLists always appends. They appeared at 0.00 in the reproduction, but they are appended unconditionally by design (ReportOptions.ts:398-400, 403-405) and are governed by the showUncategorized and showOffBudget flags, not by the category selection. They survive the narrowing by construction; AC-9 asserts they are still present so that an implementer does not extend the narrowing to them.

Payee and Account splits. They are not affected by this defect - groupBySelections builds those axes from `payees`/`accounts` (ReportOptions.ts:453-465), which carry no category selection - so no change to them is needed and none is claimed.

The two React 'Encountered two children with the same key' console warnings. They reproduce on the untouched page before any interaction, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this bug - filing them here would bury this fix.

Renaming the user-facing string 'Show empty rows'. The reporter called it 'show unused rows', but the label in the running app is 'Show empty rows' and matches its tooltip ('Show rows that are zero or blank'). The label is accurate; only the interaction with selection is wrong.
The `Sort` control defaulting to 'Budget' rather than 'Descending' in the reproduction. Noted while observing the sidebar; unrelated to this defect and not investigated.
assumptions: Dropping a group whose categories are all filtered out, rather than rendering it at 0.00, is the intended reading of the reporter's request. The reporter asks to 'even show empty rows in that group', i.e. empty rows within the selection, which is only consistent with hiding groups outside it, and it matches the sidebar's 'Hide unchecked' control. The ticket does not state a boundary for the synthetic block, which is why that is left alone rather than decided here.

filterCategoriesByConditions is the intended narrowing helper. Its semantics match what is needed - it understands both condition fields and carries the conservative fallback - and its existing use on the Budgeted path shows the codebase already treats it as the canonical answer to this question. If a maintainer prefers a different helper, the diagnosis and the reproduction still hold; only the approach would change.

Passing the unfiltered categories to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData while narrowing only the axis is correct, because the query needs the full list to evaluate the condition itself. This follows from makeQuery applying the conditions as a filter.

The narrowed {list, grouped} pair is safe to hand to categoryLists even though its two halves are no longer verbatim derivable from each other. categoryLists only uses `grouped` to look up sort_order/is_income for sorting `list` (lines 389-393), so narrowing both consistently does not disturb the sort.
unknowns: Whether unchecking a category has always produced this, or whether it is a regression. Git history here is a single squashed import commit ('Import actualbudget/actual at 3ef90fe'), so git log -S and git blame cannot date the change or reveal its original intent. The upstream issue reports it as filed 2024-10-14 and still open, which suggests long-standing rather than recent, but that is the reporter's account, not something the repository confirms.

Whether maintainers would want unselected categories hidden, or want the empty rows limited to the selected group. The reporter's intent is unambiguous - 'even show empty rows in that group' - and hiding unselected rows is the only reading consistent with the sidebar's 'Hide unchecked' control, but the exact intended boundary for the synthetic Uncategorized/Off budget block is not stated anywhere in the ticket, so it is left untouched rather than decided here.
